dossiers.catalyst_stack: On April 30, 2026 Apple posted a record March-quarter beat and authorized a $100 billion buyback, then printed another June-quarter beat on July 30 with $109.4 billion of revenue. The September 9 Surprise and Shine event launched iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max and the $1,999 foldable Duo, and Duo pre-orders opened October 16 into reportedly strong demand even after Nikkei said Pro component orders were cut at least 15% on October 9. Leadership passed from Cook to Ternus on September 1 as planned, X/SpaceXAI dropped Apple from an antitrust case on September 14, and on October 14 a judge signaled likely injunctive relief versus OpenAI. Offsetting that, a September 25 jury awarded Taction $5.72 billion on haptic patents, Ternus called the memory-chip shortage an absolute crisis on October 15, and Jefferies/KeyBanc remain structurally bearish under a $343 tape.
dossiers.key_assumption: Duo demand and Services mix offset iPhone 18 Pro order cuts and memory-cost inflation, and the Taction verdict is stayed or cut on appeal rather than paid at face value before the next print.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On June 1, 2026 Alphabet announced an $80 billion equity raise, including a $10 billion Berkshire Hathaway placement, to fund AI infrastructure, then on June 5 contracted SpaceX for about 110,000 NVIDIA GPUs at $920 million per month through June 2029. Q1 and Q2 prints on April 29 and July 22 beat revenue as Google Cloud scaled to $20.0 billion then $24.8 billion, with 2026 capex guided to $195–$205 billion, while Gemini 3.5 Flash (May 19), Gemini 4 Argon (September 30/October 13), and Universal Cart (October 15) extended the AI product cycle. A September 2 federal ruling rejected a DOJ bid to force an ad-tech breakup, Hassabis moved to Chair/Chief Scientist on August 5, and JPMorgan lifted its target to $425 on October 15. The EU Court of Justice on July 2 upheld the €4.125 billion Android fine and the Commission on July 23 levied an €890 million DMA penalty, leaving behavioral U.S. remedies and European fines as the live legal overhang.
dossiers.key_assumption: AI/Cloud demand converts the $195–$205B 2026 capex plan and the SpaceX GPU lease into revenue without a lasting FCF air-pocket, and U.S. search/ad-tech remedies stay behavioral rather than default bans or a breakup.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On July 29, 2026 Microsoft reported $90.0 billion of Q4 revenue, Azure above $100 billion for the year, and FY2027 double-digit growth guidance, extending the April 29 beat. Capacity and silicon plans stayed aggressive, including the September 10 26 GW AI-datacenter roadmap, the October 12 Maia 300 inference chip, and the October 16 NiSource 1.1 GW power deal. Offsetting that, the UK CMA on October 16 proposed Strategic Market Status in business software after the May 14 probe, and the Trump administration on October 8 suspended Microsoft from PERM. The near-term tape was mixed: Melius upgraded to Buy/$665 on October 5 against same-week cuts, Meta enterprise-AI headlines hit on October 19, and Microsoft walked away from Nscale's Loughton site on October 18.
dossiers.key_assumption: Azure/AI demand fills the announced gigawatts so capex does not become a utilization write-down, and the CMA SMS process stays a consultation through February 2027 rather than an immediate structural remedy to Office/Windows/cloud licensing.
